narrative:
The model estimates about a 26 in 100 chance that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but under the school’s decision rule it is high enough to place you in the fail group and require remedial courses, so treat it as an early warning.

The strongest signal in your profile is your record of no past class failures, which counts in your favor and pushes toward passing. The next most important signal is your father’s education level: it is primary school, and among students who passed only about 14% had fathers at that level, compared with about 33% at 5th–9th grade. This was the main factor pushing toward failing. Your weekend alcohol use, rated low, is the third most important signal and works in your favor, though less strongly; very low use is most common among passers. Although two of these top three work in your favor, the father’s-education signal plus the combined effect of smaller factors was enough for the cautious fail classification. Your sex, age and health were not used in this decision.

To improve, protect your no-failure record by keeping absences at zero and building a steadier study routine beyond two to five hours weekly. You currently do not receive family educational support, while most passers do, so ask your mother or another guardian for regular help. Keep weekend drinking very low and use school or internet resources to address weak subjects early.
